state_summary: Round 2 reports 397 observed records, 2933 eligible candidates and no pending or validation/test records. Latest measurements strengthen graph-specific pyridyl-carbonyl transfer concerns, reject several predicted solvent-response reversals, and weaken the interpretation of m73's original anomaly as reproducible chemistry. Current predictions have adapted around acquired labels, while loading sensitivity remains weak. The objective remains overall Row V1/V2 accuracy after retraining.

important_observations.measured_evidence: At identical 111.4 mg loading and DCM 300 uL, 3-pyridyl ketone m66 measures 18.98/55.06 mL at 2/1 and 47.37/119.31 at 5/1 (4659b6752f23c0b85f08; 49201b5817f204116f7f). Historical endpoint errors were -12.48/-41.00 and -35.90/-92.12 mL. Quinoline m216 reaches 53.42/92.93 at 10/1 (e47aebe2660b9e1528de), rejecting its previously predicted decline beyond 5/1.
important_observations.revision: Earlier quinoline supervision did not ensure prospective transfer to pyridyl ketone. Accurate earlier aminobenzonitrile prediction and moderate measured aminoester m86 retention still oppose a uniform nitrogen correction. Ring-N/carbonyl connectivity and eluent response deserve separate attention.

important_model_behaviors: CURRENT PREDICTIONS: At measured m92 2/1 physical inputs, 9768d61b571fc0c5ce1a predicts 6.917/12.455 at 57.75 mg and b7880e59ff4586b29a28 predicts 6.916/12.510 at 173.25 mg. CURRENT QUANTILES: Ordering defects persist. For m124 candidate df71c07fd931cc29213b, V1 q10/q50/q90 are approximately 18.05/19.30/17.40 mL. Quantile width alone cannot establish confidence.

Pyridyl ester m90 at 5/1, 166.05 mg/DCM 300 uL predicts 46.45/106.71; its matched measured pure-EA anchor is 6.71/14.27. These address eluent response and ketone-to-ester transfer within pyridyl chemistry.

Unmeasured para-chlorobenzophenone m176 at fixed 100 mg/DCM 600 uL predicts 6.31/15.81 at 5/1 and 12.02/25.06 at 20/1. It supplies ordinary aromatic-carbonyl supervision and substituent-transfer information near represented benzophenones.

Methoxynaphthalene m124 at 20/1, 53.2 mg/DCM 400 uL predicts 19.30/19.54, versus its matched measured 10/1 anchor of 6.28/12.49. This tests pronounced onset delay and interval compression. Historical m126 failure motivates scrutiny, while genuinely narrow measured intervals elsewhere prevent declaring this prediction wrong in advance.

possible_model_blind_spots: GENERAL CHEMICAL KNOWLEDGE: Increasing EA usually strengthens normal-phase elution. Pyridine-like nitrogen, sulfoxide oxygen and accessible hydroxyls can interact strongly with silica. Conjugation, steric accessibility and possible intramolecular hydrogen bonding can modify interactions. These priors motivate comparisons but do not explain the trajectory's unusual labels by themselves.

UNTESTED HYPOTHESES: Weak molecule-by-condition interactions, adsorption accessibility, dissolution and injection effects contribute to discrepancies. Shared TPSA and HBD/HBA totals cannot uniquely encode these distinctions.

Conflicting or unusual anchors may produce artificial response extrema or interval compression. The failed m73 near-repeat makes this concern concrete without identifying the cause of any unmeasured curve.
Completion-specific failure can coexist with reasonable onset prediction, as m194 showed historically. A common endpoint offset would miss that error structure.
coverage_or_redundancy_concerns: Distinct eligible IDs frequently encode identical complete physical inputs, including observed inputs. Replication is informative when tied to a specific ambiguity; catalog multiplicity and tiny density-derived mass differences do not independently add chemical coverage. Ordinary aromatic, ester, ketone and aldehyde conditions remain relevant to the Row objective alongside difficult polar graphs.
warnings: Candidate endpoint values above are current predictions only. Measured evidence comes from observed-table records; repeated memory summaries are not additional measurements.
V2 minus V1 is elution interval width. Predictive quantile width is separate and is not established uncertainty.
Historical residuals come from adaptively selected experiments before different retraining steps. They do not estimate overall Row error or establish retraining improvement.
